title: Clarify and stabilize embeddings similarity semantics: explicit metric flag + implicit-norm handling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Customers have reported small but meaningful changes in reranking and nearest-neighbor behavior after model upgrades and SDK changes. Root cause analysis showed a mix of behavior across the stack: some components were returning L2-normalized vectors, others returned raw logits-like vectors, and downstream clients assumed cosine similarity by default. This produced inconsistent results (different top-k, score ordering) and made it hard to reason about A/B and rollouts. Impact: Quality regression risk for reranking and recall-sensitive flows; customer confusion during model swaps; potential billing/monitoring mismatches when unit semantics differ. Goals: 1) Make similarity semantics explicit in the embeddings API (allow callers to request cosine or dot) 2) Provide a compatibility-preserving default that matches current hosted behavior for existing SDKs 3) Ensure server-side normalization is well-specified and optimized for latency 4) Add telemetry to detect mixed-norm payloads and help customers migrate 5) Offer a migration path and docs for customers who need deterministic cosine semantics Proposal summary: - API: introduce a stable query parameter/field "metric" with allowed values ["cosine","dot"]. Default="dot_legacy" for this release (keeps current behavior). Add optional boolean "normalize_output" for callers that want server-normalized embeddings for downstream dot-product comparisons. - Server: implement a cheap L2 normalization kernel that can operate in-place on the output buffer to avoid extra allocations. Normalize path uses vectorized kernels on CPU/GPU depending on instance. - SDKs: add explicit flag passthrough and a deprecation warning when relying on implicit semantics. - Backwards compatibility: default remains existing endpoint semantics for 30 days after release, then default will be switched to explicit "dot" with clear deprecation windows; we will not change customer data or stored vectors. - Telemetry: emit events when we detect non-unit-norm embeddings returned from model embeddings or when callers request a metric that mismatches the stored index metric. - Testing: unit + integration tests for numeric parity and an e2e rerank harness to measure ordering stability across variations. Performance constraints: in our perf microbenchmarks the in-place normalize kernel adds 0.6–1.8ms per 1K-d vector on GPU for batch sizes 1–8; for CPU the cost is higher at small batches but tolerable when batched. We will include an opt-out so latency-sensitive callers can keep raw vectors and compute normalization client-side if desired.
tasks: Design API surface and OpenAPI spec: add "metric" enum and "normalize_output" boolean
Implement normalization kernel (GPU first, then CPU) with in-place semantics
Add server-side switch to preserve legacy default behavior and feature flag for new defaults
Update python/js SDKs to accept metric/normalize flags and add warnings
Add telemetry and alerting for mixed-norm detection and customer-facing migration dashboard
Write unit tests for numeric equivalence (cosine via normalization vs explicit cosine calculation)
Create e2e rerank harness and run on 10 representative datasets to measure ordering differences
Author migration docs and in-console notice for customers with stored indexes
acceptance_criteria: API accepts "metric" and "normalize_output" parameters; schema validated in OpenAPI
Normalization kernel passes deterministic correctness tests across float16/float32 and quantized paths
No >=5% P50 latency regression on typical hosted workload when normalize_output=false
Telemetry surfaces at least two customers with mixed-norm issues during dogfood run
SDKs emit deprecation warnings for implicit assumptions and include example migration guide
Migration docs and in-console notice published before altering default behavior
notes: Trade-offs: Server-side normalization simplifies client code and reduces user errors, but it adds CPU/GPU work and risk of latency regressions for P50 sensitive workloads. To mitigate, normalization is optional and we recommend configuring batch sizes for better amortized cost. We also considered auto-detecting and normalizing only when necessary, but that adds complexity and could mask customer intent. Implementation details: the kernel uses a two-pass reduce (sum squares -> rsqrt) with numerics safeguards (epsilon clamp). For quantized paths we'll use precomputed scaling where possible. Index compatibility: we will not rewrite customer indices; instead the reranking/nearest-neighbor layer will detect metric differences and apply normalization at query time if needed.
risks: Performance regression for small-batch, low-latency callers if normalize_output=true is used naively
Customer confusion if default behavior changes without coordinated notices
Edge cases: zero vectors (all zeros) need documented fallback (return zeros and cosine defined as 0)
migration_plan: Phase 0 (dogfood): implement feature behind flag; run internal services and a subset of customers to collect telemetry (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (opt-in): SDKs expose metric flag; docs/console guidance published; default still legacy (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (notify): in-console banners and emails to customers using embeddings, provide one-click opt-in to normalized vectors (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (default switch): change default to explicit "dot" semantics documented in release notes; maintain fallback for 90 days and then fully remove legacy alias (8 weeks)
Rollback plan: revert feature flag and switch default back if >5% customer-visible ordering regressions detected
benchmarks: GPU normalize kernel: +0.6ms (1K-d, batch=1) to +1.8ms (1K-d, batch=8) median
CPU normalize kernel: +4–10ms at small batches, amortized <1ms at batch>=16
E2E rerank ordering delta: median top-5 Jaccard change 0.02 between dot_legacy and explicit dot, 0.18 between dot_legacy and cosine_normalized on sample datasets
